verdict.rationale: Next.js's own documentation says it streams UI from the server through the App Router and React Suspense, and that components can be added without sending more client-side JavaScript. That covers the core of streaming server-rendered content before client code arrives, and community reports confirm SSR works out of the box. The evidence is homepage-level marketing claims, though, so missing for 10: in-depth docs on streaming mechanics (e.g., loading boundaries, progressive flushing), evidence of perceived-load gains, and independent hands-on corroboration of streaming specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream server-rendered content so pages get faster perceived loads before all client code arrives

citations.quote: Instantly stream UI from the server, integrated with the App Router and React Suspense.
Add components without sending additional client-side JavaScript.
SSR plus SPA rendering out of the box
